was: This step explains the three kinds of sand on the beach, and with them almost every way a dam can fail.
now: What water does instead was worked out by Karl Terzaghi. By the end of this chapter it explains why water can make the castle stronger, why a heap under still water keeps its slope, the 19° face the beach chapter left unexplained, and the number every later chapter uses to say whether a slope will stand.
why: Overclaim: effective stress does not explain dams that fail by overtopping, which the book treats separately.

was: When the gaps are full of water, the water pushes on every grain from all sides, like the cushion under the block.
now: The water in the gaps meets almost all of the surface, and it presses on all of it with its own pore pressure; the water therefore carries u of each square metre's σ, and only the rest is left for the grains to carry.
why: Pore pressure does not push grains apart or outward; it carries part of the load the grains would otherwise carry between them.
